Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: The user wants to log food items. They mention 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Also earlier they had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. We need to log each item. The function log_food expects food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type optional, log_date optional. We need to call the function twice? Actually four items: frozen mango pieces, chai tea, pepperoni pizza slices, coffee. We need to decide portion units: pieces for mango, slice for pizza, maybe cup for tea and coffee? The user didn't specify meal times. We can default to snack. But we might want to ask for meal type? The instruction says we should not ask for clarification. So we should log with default meal_type snack. For log_date, we can use current date/time? We can set log_date to now. But we don't have current date/time. We can use ISO 8601 format. Let's assume now is 2026-07-29T12:00:00Z. We'll log each item. We'll call function four times.
